beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Champ, which tabletop has more room? We are looking straight down at their tops.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The long one. It reaches farther!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Area is how much flat space a shape covers. We need to measure all that space.

do.meaning: How much flat space a shape covers.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Cover both tops with equal square sticky notes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One note goes in the corner. One.

do.text: One square note is our unit.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The next note overlaps the first.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: That bit of table is covered twice!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Slide it until their edges meet. Two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The third note leaves a gap.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: There's table showing between them!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: That space has not been measured. Close the gap. Three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six. One whole row.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Start the next row at the left. Seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every bit covered exactly once. The area is twelve sticky notes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Use those same size notes on the wider top. Count across each row.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: one, two, three, four, five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Fifteen sticky notes! More than twelve, even though this table is shorter.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: It has more area. Count every square, including the ones away from the edge.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A length unit measures along a line.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Make a square with every side one unit long. This is a unit square.

do.meaning: A square with sides 1 unit long.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Its whole inside covers one square unit of area.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: If each side is one centimeter, it covers one square centimeter. Feet, inches, and meters have square units too.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each grid square covers one square unit. Count only the shaded shape.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: I'll mark them row by row, so I don't lose my place.

do.text: Mark each square as you count.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: one, two.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: three, four, five, six.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: seven, eight, nine, and ten.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten square units. In practice, tap squares to mark them, then enter the area.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This shape has a hole. Does the empty middle count?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: No. It isn't shaded.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: one, two, three, four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: five, six, seven, eight.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: nine, ten, eleven, twelve.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Twelve square units. The whole box holds sixteen squares, but four belong to the hole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here are twelve squares in a rectangle. Watch the same squares move.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: These two slide up. These two slide beside the next row.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A staircase! Did the area change?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: No. They're the same twelve squares, just moved.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Twelve square units, because we counted squares. Twelve units would describe a length.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which covering measures its tray: top, middle, or bottom? Each uses equal square cards.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The bottom. The top has a gap. The middle has an extra card on top of others.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Only the bottom covers every bit exactly once. Six square cards, so its area is six square cards.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What if we cover the long table with smaller sticky notes? Each side is half as long.

do.text: Would that give a smaller number?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Would that give a smaller number?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Look closely at one old note. One small note covers only this corner.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two fill the top. Three, four fill the bottom. Four small notes cover one large note.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: We need more of them, because each covers less space.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each of the twelve large notes is replaced by four small ones.

do.text: Four small notes replace one large note.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four in every space. Twelve groups of four make forty eight small notes.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The table didn't grow. Just the count!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Smaller squares take more. Switch back to larger squares, and you need fewer. Always name the unit with the number.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: With the same size notes, twelve on the long top and fifteen on the wider top.

do.text: Compare using the same size square.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The wider one has more room!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Cover it with equal squares, no gaps, no overlaps, and count.

do.text: Equal squares. No gaps. No overlaps.
